A 1,971 kg silver bar is being tokenized in Dubai.

And honestly, my first thought was… who is actually going to buy this?

Because buying a physical silver bar comes with lots of hassle, like storage, security and,

obviously, the amount of money and it involves.

But that's the best part of tokenization.
The silver stays physically stored, while ownership can be divided into smaller digital units.

So instead of needing to buy the entire bar, investors can potentially get exposure to a fraction of it.

But it’s not just about putting an asset on a blockchain.

It’s about making assets that are difficult to access more accessible.

The more I looked into this, the more interesting it became.

You’re not necessarily buying a digital asset with nothing behind it.

The idea is that there’s a real physical asset sitting in custody behind the token.

Of course, the actual custody, legal rights and structure matter.

You still have to do your homework and should get the right consultation before putting money into it.

But honestly, this is where RWA tokenization starts making a lot more sense to me.

Would you consider owning a fraction of a physical silver bar?

#silverbar #tokenization #realworldasset #fractionalownership #digitalasset #Dubai #India

This photo, 13 years ago.

She's in Saudi Arabia now. I'm in India.

me and my sister, Zuberiya Nauman, at a mall window at 1am, waiting for our parents to finish up.

last night.
No camera, just a phone call.

2am for me, 12 for her 

she was out on a walk, on the other side of the world, still talking to me.

13 years and two countries apart.

Same two sisters, same window, basically.

On that call, half-asleep, we said something out loud we'd both been circling for months.

We're both LinkedIn content writers.

We'd never said this to each other before.

Every industry has a problem so common insiders stopped noticing it.

So normal, nobody thought to call it out. So unspoken, nobody's written it down.

We'd both spent months finding that problem in other people's industries. Neither of us had said it about our own.

Content writing has the exact same unspoken thing. Everyone posts tips. Nobody says the real reason most posts fail: the writer never sat still long enough to hear what their reader was already complaining about.

That's not a writing gap. It's a listening gap.

So that's what we do now - the whole job is what we were doing on that windowsill 13 years ago, before either of us called it a skill.

Actually listening, long enough to hear the thing nobody's said yet.

If your posts get seen and forgotten, it's not a writing problem.
Nobody's said your industry's unspoken thing yet.

We're Khadeejah Nauman and Zuberiya — sisters, LinkedIn content writers.

Comment "LISTEN" and I'll tell you the one unspoken thing in your industry nobody's written down yet.

They sell ₹25 lakh packages.
but they want - lead generation for free.
Well…

“On commission.” 😂

I recently got a lead generation request from a company selling services starting at around ₹25 lakh.

Big company.

High-ticket service.

Lead generation budget? ₹0.

They wanted me to handle the research, prospecting, list building, outreach, follow-ups and meeting generation…

…and get paid only if they closed a deal.

This is where I think businesses misunderstand lead generation.

A ₹25 lakh deal doesn't appear because you sent 20 LinkedIn requests.
Someone has to consistently:

→ Find the right ICP
→ Research decision-makers
→ Build the prospect list
→ Run outreach
→ Follow up
→ Test messaging
→ Expand into new markets

Every. Single. Day.

And here's the funny part:

Their own profile was positioned around lead generation. 😂

So basically:

“We help businesses generate leads.”

Also:
“Please generate leads for us for free.”

Kya gira? Dikhao. 😂

Commission can work.

But it shouldn't mean someone else finances your entire lead-generation process with their time.

If one client is worth ₹25 lakh,
lead generation shouldn't have a ₹0 budget.

If you are also dealing with similar client drop your experience in comments 

and if you are genuinely want to explore Lead genration for your business 
drop "hey" in comment

I spent 3 hours confused about a podcast term. It changed how I invest.

Fractional ownership isn’t about owning parts of a house or car. It’s about owning parts of any asset art, real estate, even intellectual property via digital tokens.

In 2025, Raj Shamani and Dr. Abdulnasser explained it on a podcast. I didn’t get it. So I dug into Web3 and tokenization.

Here’s the catch: These tokens are digital. They’re unregulated in most places. That’s why compliance felt impossible.

Then I found companies. They handle the legal hoops. They let you buy tiny pieces of assets you couldn’t afford alone.

What asset would you fractionalize first? Drop it in the comments. Let’s figure this out together. 💰

POV: You stopped treating LinkedIn like a place to post. You started treating it like a place to learn.

For a long time, I'd open LinkedIn thinking about what I should post.

Now, I open it with a different goal.

I scroll.

I read the entire post.

I try to understand why it worked.

Was it a story?

A framework?

A controversial opinion?

A personal experience?

Only after understanding the context do I decide whether I have something valuable to add.

I don't comment on every post.

I comment only when I can contribute a new perspective or ask a thoughtful question.

Sometimes that comment becomes a conversation.

Sometimes it brings profile visits.

Sometimes it turns into an inbound lead.

The goal isn't to leave 100 comments.

The goal is to leave the one comment people remember.

That's when LinkedIn stopped feeling like a platform I had to feed...

...and started becoming a platform that fed my pipeline.
